title: Rabbi Shimon bar Nezira
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Shabbat 33b, concerning the statement that Rabbi Gurion — and some say Rav Yosef bar Shemaya — said, about the time when righteous people are present in the generation: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Zeira said, and some say Rabbi Shimon ben Nezira, what is the verse? Etc. And in Yevamot 97a, Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: Whenever a Torah scholar has a teaching said in his name in this world, his lips (etc.). Rabbi Yitzchak ben Zeira said, and some say Shimon Nezira, what is the verse? Etc. This statement is also brought in Shekalim, end of chapter 2: Shimon ben Nezira in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak said: Any Torah scholar etc. And in the Jerusalem Talmud, Moed Katan chapter 3, end of halakhah 7: Bar Tira said, one who says a teaching in someone's name, his lips move in the grave etc. Hyman proposes without doubt that it should read Bar Nezira, and from nun and zayin a tet was made.

Hyman concludes from this that Bar Nezira is Rabbi Shimon bar Nezira, and under this name we find him in Shekalim, end of chapter 2: Bar Nezira says, like someone drinking spiced wine (konditon)…; Rabbi Yitzchak says, like that etc.
And he is likewise mentioned by this name in Song of Songs Rabbah 1:14.
And he is mentioned in Shabbat, chapter 2, halakhah 3: Rabbi Acha, Rabbi Simon in the name of Rabbi Shimon Nezira: If he made it into a bandage, it is ritually pure, etc.

notes.text: In the named Shekalim2:5 paragraph, deshatei means someone who drinks spiced wine. In Shabbat2:3, mazzor is a bandage and the ruling declares it pure. Hyman’s proposed nun-zayin/tet copying error remains conjectural.

The consulted Shekalim 2:5 paragraph names Shimon ben Nezira reporting Yitzchak and Bar Nezira drinking konditon. Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:3 names Shimon Nezira and rules that material made into a bandage is pure. Neither passage independently proves Hyman’s Bar Tira emendation or identity argument.
